title: Okta application assignment state
description: One record per Okta-registered application capturing which groups are entitled to access it, its classification, and whether its app sign-in policy requires MFA. Pulled on a schedule from /api/v1/apps, /api/v1/apps/{id}/groups, /api/v1/policies/{policyId}/rules and /api/v1/policies?type=OKTA_SIGN_ON. The platform evaluator decides pass/fail per (control, assignment) pair; the connector emits descriptive (INCONCLUSIVE) records. 1.1.0 (#2828) adds classification, sign_on_policy_id, sign_on_mfa_required and reason; a field the connector has no value for is omitted. 1.2.0 (#2951) decides AUTH_METHOD_CHAIN rules in sign_on_mfa_required and adds session_mfa_required and session_reason, from the org's global session policy.

app_id.description: Okta application id (the OKTA assigned UUID-like identifier).

sign_on_mode.description: Okta sign-on mode (SAML_2_0, OPENID_CONNECT, BOOKMARK, SECURE_PASSWORD_STORE, AUTO_LOGIN, etc.).

assigned_group_ids.description: Group ids that are entitled to access the application.

assigned_group_count.description: Cardinality of assigned_group_ids (denormalized for evaluator convenience).

classification.description: The operator's classification of the app, from the connector's --admin-apps and --infrastructure-apps app-id lists; every other app is standard. Omitted when the operator classified no app.

sign_on_policy_id.description: Id of the app sign-in policy (ACCESS_POLICY) the app's _links.accessPolicy names. Omitted when the app has none (a Classic Engine org, or an API service app with no policy assigned).

sign_on_mfa_required.description: True when every active rule of the app sign-in policy denies access, or allows it with an ASSURANCE verification method whose factorMode is 2FA or an AUTH_METHOD_CHAIN whose every sign-in path presents two factor classes; false when an active rule allows 1FA or has a one-class chain path. Omitted when undecided, with reason saying why.

session_mfa_required.description: Whether the org's global session policy (OKTA_SIGN_ON) requires MFA for every user: true when every reachable active rule denies access or sets requireFactor; false when a reachable active rule allows a session without it. The same for every app of one connector run. Omitted when undecided, with session_reason saying why.
